text:
maya: heads up — running into weird behavior with header-driven model aliasing + pinning. If a route has both `X-Model-Alias` and an explicit `model_pin`, the evaluator sometimes ignores the pin and returns a compatible fallback instead.
kevin: hmm can you paste the route config and a repro request?
maya: gist of route:
```
route {
  match: path = /v1/generate
  headers: { X-Model-Alias: /gptx-.*/ }
  model_pin: "gptx-2024-04"
  compatibility: { require: cpu_quantized }
}
```
Request has X-Model-Alias: gptx-2024-04-beta. The runtime returns `gptx-2023-small` (compatible) instead of honoring the `model_pin`.
adele: that's surprising — pin should supersede alias match. Are we applying pin at the right stage of selection?
kevin: suspect the evaluator pipeline applies alias-to-candidate expansion, then compatibility filter, then selects best candidate by cost. If `model_pin` is stored as a separate override it may be evaluated later and ignored if pinned model fails compatibility check.
liam: why would pinned model fail compatibility here? It's the same family. Any telemetry showing why `gptx-2024-04` considered incompatible?
maya: logs show: "candidate gptx-2024-04 rejected: kernel_missing:int8_avx2" then we fall back to nearest compatible.
sophie: that kernel_missing is from compilation/kernel-selection — pinned model might need kernel build for the host. But expected behavior when pin is explicit is to *fail* request (or fall back only if fallback policy allows), not silently pick a different family model.
kevin: agree. Current policy enum is { honor_pin, allow_compat_fallback }. Default was allow_compat_fallback historically to keep apps alive. Maybe we changed default in rollout inadvertently.
maya: can we add explicit flag in route DSL so teams can pick: `pin_policy: STRICT | RELAXED`? STRICT = error if pinned model unavailable. RELAXED = allow compatibility fallback.
liam: from UX side console should show when a route is RELAXED and a fallback occurred. Right now the dashboard only shows final model used, not the reason. Need telemetry: pinned_model, pinned_status (OK/REJECTED), fallback_model, reject_reason.
adele: +1 telemetry. Also we should emit an event tag for rollouts: `pin_overrode_alias` or `alias_overrode_pin` so we can query regressed apps.
kevin: implementation plan:
1) evaluator: short-circuit on pin if pin_policy==STRICT -> either select pin or raise ModelUnavailableError.
2) pin_policy==RELAXED -> expand alias and do compatibility filter, but *emit* telemetry about pin rejection and fallback.
3) add unit tests for kernel_missing path and for mixed header+pin cases.
sophie: also update feature flag controls; we used a FF when flipping default earlier — check `ff-routing-pin-default` and make sure migration set for new default won't flip behavior unexpectedly.
maya: can we also add a small change to routing DSL so header match can include `alias_match_type: exact|prefix|regex`? Some users rely on fuzzy matches and pin interacts badly.
kevin: yep. I'll sketch patch and attach tests.
adele: note for console: we should surface a small timeline for each route showing last 7 pin rejections with reasons. That should help customers debug kernel/quantization issues.
liam: and quota interaction: if fallback model is cheaper, request could pass quota checks differently — we must ensure quota enforcement happens after selection or at least we record original pinned-model cost expectation. Otherwise quota alerts will be noisy.
kevin: good point — quota check currently uses selected_model. We should tag quota logs with `requested_model` vs `selected_model`.
deploy-bot: Deploy starting: routing-evaluator-pin-policy v2 -> canary 4 pods in eu-west-1 at 11:47 UTC :rocket:
maya: thanks — will watch telemetry and screenshots of console. If canary shows increased pin_reject events we can roll back.
sophie: I'll review FF state and add a migration note.
maya: thanks all — filing follow-up bug with details and linking this thread. :seedling:
